title: From 46% to 90%: Fine-Tuning Tiny LLMs for On-Device Agents — Cormac Brick, Google
talk_summary: Cormac Brick describes Google's on-device AI stack: a simple skill harness where only skill descriptions are in the prompt and full skill details load on demand, plus tiny LLM deployment via LiteRT-LM. He shows that fine-tuning a 270M Function Gemma with synthetic data raised narrow function-calling success from 46% to over 90% for most functions, and notes small models handle about eight skills but struggle with multi-skill single answers.

takeaways.what_they_do: Put only skill names/descriptions in the system prompt; the model calls a load-skill tool to fetch full instructions and function details only when needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the model is aware of the types of skills it can use, but it doesn't have to see all of the functions and details of the skill

takeaways.technique: Synthetic-data fine-tuning for narrow tool calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Generate a synthetic dataset with Flash for specific app functions, then fine-tune a tiny Function Gemma model instead of relying on a large model prompt with all function schemas.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We use flash to synthetically create a data set.

takeaways.technique: Cap active skills and orchestrate multi-step calls explicitly
takeaways.what_they_do: They enable about eight skills by default; the small model chooses among them reasonably well, but calling multiple skills in one answer is still unreliable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: by default we enable about eight skills and it's able to choose between the eight skills reasonably well

takeaways.technique: Agents author and test skills in sandbox
takeaways.what_they_do: They use Gemini CLI/Code Coach to write skills and an ADB skill to debug and test them on a device, so skills can be generated and validated by coding agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can use skills to write skills

takeaways.technique: Chain tiny specialized models for preprocessing
takeaways.what_they_do: They chain a small ASR model with a small text-polishing model to produce offline transcription with personalization and removal of filler words.
takeaways.evidence_quote: chained together they can create a really compelling offline like offline transcription service
